minutes.headline: Parks Commission took no vote to open the beach and set a mid-July decision point, meeting again June 13 at 6 p.m.
minutes.summary: The remote Parks Commission meeting was mostly about whether the Memorial Beach could safely open under COVID-19 guidelines, with concerns over distancing, cleaning supplies and staffing. No decision to open was made; members agreed to revisit in July and to consider swim lessons later. The DPW director and recreation director also updated on fields, Marshall Park bathroom demolition, the Wallace Park court, and a broken playground merry-go-round.

Offered Board of Health help expediting answers; next Board of Health meeting June 15; will be on the board until June 22.

Past rate increases made beach programs cover their costs, so a lessons-only program could be self-funded.
Professional disinfecting and supplies would carry cost and timing questions, and supplies would not arrive until end of June.
Procurement, demo permit and hazardous materials survey are in late stages.

decisions.decision: No decision to open the beach; commissioners not comfortable opening now.
Agreed to reconsider the beach and possible swim lessons in July, with a mid-July decision point.
Fields remain open; the recreation director may start organized activity once state requirements are met, without further commission approval.
Next meeting set for Monday the 13th at 6:00 p.m., with the beach on the agenda.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission made no decision to open Memorial Beach, with commissioners not comfortable opening under current COVID-19 conditions.
Members agreed to reconsider the beach and possible swim lessons in July, with a mid-July decision point.
Fields stay open, and the recreation director may start organized activity once state requirements are met, without further commission approval.
The DPW director reported that procurement, demolition permit and hazardous materials survey for the old Marshall Park bathroom are in late stages.
The next meeting was set for Monday the 13th at 6:00 p.m., with the beach on the agenda.

why_it_matters: Residents will not have the town beach this early summer, and any swim lessons depend on a July decision that turns on distancing, cleaning supplies and staffing.
A lessons-only program could be paid for by user fees rather than the town budget, since past rate increases made beach programs cover their costs.
